bug_semantics: CWE-639 IDOR on the shared authenticated download endpoint. routes/common.php registers GET uploads/{id}/download as Common\Uploads@download behind only auth (no admin/portal permission). download() does Media::find($id) and streams the file. Media uses the Tenants/Company global scope, so cross-company rows are filtered, but there is no object-level check that a portal customer owns the mediable parent. Any authenticated same-company portal user can enumerate media IDs and download other customers' invoice/bill/receipt attachments. Vendor patch 80ef6d3 added authorizeMedia()/mediaBelongsToContact(), allowing read-admin-panel users company-wide and portal users only when the parent contact_id matches the requester.
flaw_origin: The ID-keyed download without ownership was first written on 2018-01-02 in ddd18c7ea6f872540c293f40d99c987842ac0f6f ('Invoice path' by cuneytsenturk). That commit changed download($folder,$file) plus company-prefixed getPath() into download($id) with Media::find($id) and a path derived only from the media record, and simultaneously switched the shared auth route from {folder}/{file}/download to {id}/download. The client portal already existed (9710f810, 2017-10-21) and these upload routes already sat outside permission:read-admin-panel. Later try/catch (297b328), streaming helpers, and tenant scoping preserved the missing contact ownership check until 80ef6d3.

Attack path is authenticated portal access to GET {company_id}/uploads/{id}/download: download() loads Media by attacker-controlled ID and streams it. Company global scope blocks other tenants, so the live hole is same-company object-level IDOR (CVE text saying 'other company's files' is imprecise; the vendor fix comment matches the code). The smallest first-write of that ID-keyed download is ddd18c7ea6, which replaced path-based download($folder,$file) with Media::find($id) and exposed {id}/download on the shared auth route; parent 6429a699 still lacks those lines. Later commits are refactors, not BICs. 80ef6d3 is the first and direct fix (authorizeMedia), landing in 3.2.0 and absent from 3.1.21.
